summary: Preserve JavaScript call evaluation order by introducing temporaries when a direct C# expression would reorder base lookup, getter calls, or argument side effects.

target.notes: ECMAScript evaluates the callee/reference first, then argument expressions left-to-right, then invokes. C# is also left-to-right for ordinary calls, but lowering transformations must not duplicate or hoist effects across this boundary.

caveats: Property getters and Proxy traps during callee lookup are effects.
Spread operands interleave iterator effects with argument-list construction.
references: ECMAScript 2026 Language Specification EvaluateCall / ArgumentList Evaluation

tests.name: callee getter before args
tests.input: let s=[]; const o={get f(){s.push('g'); return x=>x}}; o.f((s.push('a'),1)); console.log(s.join(','));

tests.name: args left to right
tests.input: let s=[]; function f(a,b){} f((s.push(1),1),(s.push(2),2)); console.log(s.join(','));
